sections.title: Describing someone with a whole clause
sections.content: aki ("who") lets you attach a whole description to a person instead of just one adjective: valaki, aki... ("someone who..."). It's a new small word, not a new verb form — everything after aki conjugates exactly the way you already know.

items.spanish: A szomszédom olyan ember, aki sokat dolgozik.
items.english: My neighbor is someone who works a lot.

items.spanish: Ismerek egy kollégát, aki nagyon vicces.
items.english: I know a colleague who is very funny.

sections.content: ismer means "to know [a person]" specifically — ismerek egy kollégát is "I know a colleague", not "I know a fact". It conjugates exactly like any other regular verb you already know.
